msgWinUpdateWarningBody:
This setting completely disables all Windows updates.

 Suitability: May be appropriate for systems used for specific purposes that do not require active internet browsing.

 Warning: Disabling updates significantly increases the risk of the system being hacked or infected due to the lack of security patches.

 Note: It is strongly advised against using this setting due to the heightened security risks.

Disabling Windows Update is not recommended. This is only for advanced users who know what they are doing.
It also makes some features in HyperLis (such as WSAP) unable to run correctly.

Do you want to continue?

wsapDescBody:
Windows Setup Automatic Protocol (WSAP) lets you install or reinstall Windows automatically, right from your PC.
No USB required, no complicated steps” just a smooth, guided process.
Fast, simple, and reliable, so you can get back to work or play in no time.

You have selected Disk {0} to install Windows.

WSAP will automatically shrink your C: drive by 10GB to create a temporary installation environment.
All your personal data on this disk WILL BE DELETED during the final installation phase.

Are you absolutely sure you want to proceed and accept the risk of data loss?
msgWsapWarningsBody:
IMPORTANT WARNINGS:

1. Please ensure that Secure Boot is disabled in your BIOS/UEFI settings before proceeding.

2. This feature is currently unstable and should only be used when a USB Boot drive is unavailable, due to the risk of data loss or boot access errors.

3. This feature works best with official (stock) Windows images. Modified or tweaked Windows versions may not be fully supported.

Do you understand these risks and want to continue?

msgRestorePointRequiredBody:
WARNING: System Protection (Restore Point) is currently DISABLED on drive C:.

Extreme Gaming optimization deeply modifies system settings, services, and registry values. Changes may be irreversible without a System Restore Point.

To ensure system safety, you MUST enable System Protection on drive C: before proceeding.

The System Protection window will now open so you can turn on protection and click 'Create...' to create a restore point.

msgConfirmRemoveHWID:
Are you sure you want to remove Windows Digital License (HWID) activation?

• The current product key and digital certificates will be removed.
• If this PC has a factory OEM license in BIOS, it will be automatically restored.
msgConfirmRemoveWinKMS:
Are you sure you want to remove Windows Online KMS activation?

• Auto-renewal tasks and KMS script files will be completely deleted.
• The associated KMS server settings will be removed.
msgConfirmRemoveWinTSforce:
Are you sure you want to remove Windows TSforce (KMS38) activation?

• Product keys and TSforce registry overrides will be removed.
• The system activation state will be rearmed.
msgWarningOemKeyLoss: Note: Removing MAS may temporarily affect your OEM key. After completion, you must restart your computer and re-enter the OEM key to reactivate.
msgConfirmRemoveOhook:
Are you sure you want to remove Ohook activation for Microsoft Office?

• Running Office applications will be closed.
• Injected hook DLLs (sppc.dll) will be removed and original OSPPC.DLL will be restored.
msgConfirmRemoveOffTSforce:
Are you sure you want to remove TSforce activation for Microsoft Office?

• All forged Office TSforce product keys will be uninstalled.
• Office SPP registry configurations will be cleaned.
msgConfirmRemoveOffKMS:
Are you sure you want to remove Online KMS activation for Microsoft Office?

• Office KMS host settings will be cleared.
• Office KMS client product keys will be uninstalled.
